title: Things to do when bored
summary: This is a humorous list of absurd, playful, and deliberately pointless activities, arranged as a long run of short items separated by dashes. Each entry is a single line, often built on a wordplay, a dash of parody, or a surreal twist on everyday life. Examples include waxing the ceiling, playing Houdini with a sibling, learning Greek by reading Homer in the original, trying to join the Foreign Legion, sleeping on a bed of nails, and giving a Rorschach test to a gerbil. The list also pokes fun at pop culture, politics, and history, with references to Richard Nixon, Pat Boone, Three's Company, the Mansons, Ronco and K-tel, and the Cold War. Some items are clever puns, such as Ski Kansas or Be a square root, while others are sheer nonsense meant to make the reader laugh. The text reads as a single gag-driven catalogue rather than a narrative, and it is typical of the joke-book and novelty-list genre of its era.
